facts.fact: The authors state that a prototype electronic clinical record for obstetrics at the 180-bed Irene Neto Maternity Hospital in Lubango was in its test phase, with the clinical processes of deliveries from the fourth quarter of 2016 being entered retrospectively in the admission, archive and medical statistics section; the document gives no date for this, so its publication date is used.
facts.system: ObsCare prototype (electronic clinical record of obstetrics)

facts.fact: The authors state that the electronic clinical record prototype at the Irene Neto Maternity Hospital is part of a doctoral research project at the University of Beira Interior, Portugal, adapting ObsCare, an application developed at the University of Porto's Faculty of Medicine and owned by Virtual Care; no ministry role is stated, and the document gives no date, so its publication date is used.
facts.system: ObsCare prototype (electronic clinical record of obstetrics)

systems.system: ObsCare prototype (electronic clinical record of obstetrics)
systems.country_label: computerized database of clinical processes / electronic clinical record of obstetrics
systems.platform: ObsCare, owned by Virtual Care-Systems for Life, developed at the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Porto
systems.owner: doctoral research project, Faculty of Health Sciences of the University of Beira Interior, with the Faculty of Medicine of Universidade Mandume Ya Ndemufayo
systems.tiers: one hospital, the Irene Neto Maternity Hospital in Lubango, Huíla (180 beds), in the admission, archive and medical statistics section; prototype under test

note: Classed emr because the document describes the application as the hospital's electronic clinical record giving full support to gynaecological and obstetric practice, the whole work of a maternity hospital; the parent may prefer tracker (maternal). It is a prototype under test, not routine use, so no tiers or clinics fact. Also stated, without a fact: the hospital's statistics area has no application for treating its information, and a 2010 MINSA evaluation of the SIS stressed the need to computerise admission, archive and medical statistics at level II and III health units.
